proofs.proof_tex:
The already established theorem \(\mathrm{thm:qstar\text{-}uniform\text{-}risk\text{-}upper}\) proves that \(\delta_n^\star\) is total and supplies a finite \(B_c\) for which
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
\le\max_y\mathbb E[(\delta_n^\star-\tau_c(y))^2]
\le\frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+B_cn^{-3/2}.
\tag{19}
\]
The first inequality is the definition of the minimax infimum under the fixed independent design; all ratios in the procedure are supported because \(q_a^\star>0\) on \(S_c\), as proved in that theorem.

Conversely, \(\mathrm{lem:qstar\text{-}full\text{-}label\text{-}bayes\text{-}converse}\) shows that for every positive rational \(\eta\), eventually
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
\ge\frac1n-(\Lambda_c+\eta)n^{-4/3}.
\tag{20}
\]
Put
\[
e_n=n^{4/3}\left[R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
-\left\{n^{-1}-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}\right\}\right].
\]
Equations (19)--(20) give \(-\eta\le e_n\le B_cn^{-1/6}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Since this holds for every positive rational \(\eta\), one has \(e_n\to0\).  This is precisely
\[
R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
=\frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\]
Together with the first assertion of (19), this proves every clause of the theorem.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(K\ge3\) be fixed, let \(c\in\mathbb R^K\) satisfy \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}c_a=0\), \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}|c_a|=2\), and \(|S_c|\ge3\), and fix real endpoints \(L<U\). For observed bounded outcomes \((w_{i,A_i})_{i=1}^n\in[L,U]^n\), put \(z_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=(w_{i,A_i}-L)/(U-L)\) and define the mathematically total lifted estimator under the independent allocation \(q^\star\) by the finite polynomial
\[
\delta_{n,[L,U]}^\star(A,w_A)
=(U-L)\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}
 \delta_n^\star(A,x)
 \prod_{i=1}^n
 \{x_i z_i^{\mathrm{obs}}+(1-x_i)(1-z_i^{\mathrm{obs}})\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Here \(\delta_n^\star(A,x)\) means the binary procedure of \(\mathrm{def:qstar\text{-}procedure}\) evaluated at the labels \(A\) and binary observed outcomes \(x\). Then the same finite constant \(B_c\) as in \(\mathrm{thm:qstar\text{-}second\text{-}order}\) satisfies
\[
\sup_{w\in[L,U]^{n\times K}}
\mathbb E\!\left[
 \{\delta_{n,[L,U]}^\star(A,w_A)-\tau_c(w)\}^2
\right]
\le (U-L)^2\left\{
 \frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+B_cn^{-3/2}
\right\}.
\tag{2}
\]
Moreover, if \(R_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)\) denotes the minimax risk with this fixed independent design and bounded schedules, then
\[
R_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
=(U-L)^2R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)
=(U-L)^2\left\{
 \frac1n-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})
\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]
The totality in this statement is mathematical totality; it makes no exact Turing-computability assertion for unrepresented real endpoints or observations.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(d=U-L>0\). Fix a bounded schedule \(w\in[L,U]^{n\times K}\), and set
\[
z_{i,a}=\frac{w_{i,a}-L}{d}\in[0,1].
\tag{4}
\]
Conditional on this fixed schedule, introduce independent latent variables \(\Xi_{i,a}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(z_{i,a})\), independent also of the assignment and of any randomization in the binary procedure. For fixed \(A\), the conditional law of the observed latent vector \((\Xi_{i,A_i})_{i=1}^n\) is the product law with success probabilities \((z_{i,A_i})_{i=1}^n\). Consequently, expanding its finite support gives
\[
\mathbb E_{\Xi}\!\left[\delta_n^\star(A,\Xi_A)\mid A\right]
=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}\delta_n^\star(A,x)
 \prod_{i=1}^n\{x_i z_{i,A_i}+(1-x_i)(1-z_{i,A_i})\}.
\tag{5}
\]
The right side of \((5)\) is exactly the polynomial in \((1)\) and uses only \(A\) and the observed normalized values \(z_{i,A_i}=z_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\). Thus \(\delta_{n,[L,U]}^\star\) is observable from the bounded labeled data. Each factor in \((5)\) is defined also at the boundary values \(z_{i,A_i}=0\) and \(z_{i,A_i}=1\), the sum has \(2^n\) terms, and \(\delta_n^\star\) is total by \(\mathrm{thm:qstar\text{-}second\text{-}order}\); hence the lifted estimator is mathematically total.

The zero-sum assumption gives, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_c(w)
&=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}
 c_a\{L+d z_{i,a}\}\\
&=\frac Ln\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}c_a
 +\frac d n\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}c_a z_{i,a}\\
&=d\,\mathbb E_{\Xi}\!\left[\tau_c(\Xi)\right].
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
The first equality is \((4)\), the second is linearity, the third uses \(\sum_a c_a=0\) and \(\mathbb E_\Xi\Xi_{i,a}=z_{i,a}\). Because \(w\) is fixed, \((1)\), \((5)\), and \((6)\) imply, for every assignment label vector \(A\),
\[
\delta_{n,[L,U]}^\star(A,w_A)-\tau_c(w)
=d\,\mathbb E_{\Xi}\!\left[
 \delta_n^\star(A,\Xi_A)-\tau_c(\Xi)\mid A
\right].
\tag{7}
\]
For
\(Z=\delta_n^\star(A,\Xi_A)-\tau_c(\Xi)\), the elementary conditional-variance identity
\[
\mathbb E_\Xi[Z^2\mid A]-\{\mathbb E_\Xi[Z\mid A]\}^2
=\mathbb E_\Xi\!\left[
 \{Z-\mathbb E_\Xi[Z\mid A]\}^2\mid A
\right]\ge0
\]
proves conditional Jensen's inequality for the square. Applying it to \((7)\), followed by expectation over the independent assignment, yields
\[
\mathbb E_A\!\left[
 \{\delta_{n,[L,U]}^\star(A,w_A)-\tau_c(w)\}^2
\right]
\le d^2\mathbb E_{A,\Xi}\!\left[
 \{\delta_n^\star(A,\Xi_A)-\tau_c(\Xi)\}^2
\right].
\tag{8}
\]
Outcome independence is used here: the law of \(A\) is the same for every realization of the latent binary schedule \(\Xi\). Therefore the last expectation is a mixture of binary-schedule risks and is at most
\[
\max_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K}}
\mathbb E_A\!\left[
 \{\delta_n^\star(A,y_A)-\tau_c(y)\}^2
\right].
\tag{9}
\]
The established uniform upper bound \(\mathrm{thm:qstar\text{-}second\text{-}order}\), applied to \((9)\), and then the supremum over \(w\), prove \((2)\).

For the minimax identity, take in \(\mathrm{lem:multiarm\text{-}bounded\text{-}endpoint\text{-}reduction}\) the fixed design class consisting of the independent outcome-independent assignment law with probabilities \(q^\star\). That lemma preserves the same design law, arbitrary estimator randomization, and complete-label observation, and gives exactly
\[
R_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)=d^2R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c).
\tag{10}
\]
Finally, \(\mathrm{thm:qstar\text{-}second\text{-}order}\) gives
\(R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_cn^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\). Multiplication by the fixed positive constant \(d^2\) in \((10)\) proves \((3)\). No limiting or division step uses a vanishing endpoint width because \(L<U\) is fixed.
added_lemmas.justification: The exact bounded-endpoint reduction transports the sharp fixed-independent binary expansion without changing the design law, while the displayed finite polynomial supplies an explicit total attaining procedure.
added_lemmas.gap: This fixed-independent result does not establish unrestricted second-order optimality for a general permitted multiarm contrast.
added_lemmas.consumer: A trialist with a bounded fixed-horizon endpoint can prespecify the contrast-weighted independent allocation and the Rao--Blackwellized Airy procedure; exact Turing evaluation is asserted only where inputs have a representation.

proposed.def: The minimax squared-error risk over schedules in \([L,U]^{n\times K}\) when assignments are independent with probabilities \(q^\star\) and only the possibly randomized labeled-data estimator is optimized.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The separately owned bounded independent theorem needs its own risk-value notation while the fixed-class bounded game remains sibling-owned.

proposed.name: \delta_{n,[L,U]}^\star
proposed.def: The finite observed-data Bernoulli-polynomial Rao--Blackwellization of \(\delta_n^\star\), multiplied by \(U-L\), defined in \(\mathrm{thm:qstar\text{-}bounded\text{-}endpoint\text{-}second\text{-}order}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The bounded independent theorem requires explicit notation for its total finite-data attaining procedure.

prose_updates.tldr: For the unequal three-arm contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the unrestricted design--estimator game has the proved sharp expansion \(R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-C_A(5/8)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\). The contrast-weighted independent allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\) attains the same second-order coefficient, and the binary eight-type construction supplies a terminating finite-input certificate with a computable all-future error tail. An exact endpoint-reduction theorem also transports both the unrestricted three-arm result and the general fixed-independent benchmark to every fixed bounded interval \([L,U]\), multiplying risk by \((U-L)^2\). The bounded lift is mathematically total, but no exact Turing claim is made for unrepresented real endpoints or observations.

project_justification.gap: The two-arm literature solves the unrestricted binary-treatment action space, whereas it does not determine the sharp coefficient for three active arms. The proved three-arm allocation-tube theorem closes the formerly missing design-independent Bayes bridge for \(c^\dagger\), uniformly over local counts, exterior positive-count allocations, proper faces, dependent assignment laws, and randomized labeled-data estimators. The remaining mathematical gap is unrestricted sharpness for a general permitted multiarm contrast, not the fixed-independent expansion.
project_justification.niche: At \(c^\dagger\), the face-robust basis \([v,d^\dagger,\mathbf 1]\) separates target, transverse, and common-shift directions. Exact finite-population regression and directional van Trees bounds then control every allocation face, while the independent Airy feedback supplies the matching upper procedure. This yields the first sharp unrestricted three-active-arm coefficient in the note's fixed-horizon binary experiment and shows that \(q^\dagger\) has no second-order loss at this contrast.
project_justification.fill: The contribution consists of the proved eight-type face-robust all-count Bayes expansion, its lossless orbit reduction against arbitrary outcome-independent dependent designs and arbitrary randomized estimators, a matching total binary procedure, the evaluable Airy object \(C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), and a terminating rational finite-data certificate with a nonincreasing computable tail. A separate exact bounded-endpoint reduction uses an observable finite Bernoulli polynomial and conditional Jensen, preserving the design and estimator quantifiers and multiplying both minimax risks and attaining bounds by \((U-L)^2\).

prose_updates.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026), Theorems 2.2--2.3 and 3.1, optimize over the same unrestricted assignment-mechanism and measurable-estimator quantifiers for a binary-treatment action space: they prove the exact binary game, exact bounded-endpoint scaling, and its Airy expansion. Hull (2026), Theorem 1, likewise optimizes over every assignment mechanism and measurable estimator and gives the equivalent exact bounded two-arm game. Neither result covers three arms. Restricting the present three-arm nature class by \(Y(2)=Y(3)\) gives the valid comparison \(R_n(c^\dagger)\ge\rho_n^\star=n^{-1}-C_A n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\). Since \(C_A>C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), that imported two-arm converse is strictly weaker than the proved sharp three-arm coefficient. Hirano and Porter (2009) and Levit (1986) motivate limiting-decision and spectral arguments, while Bai (2023), Armstrong (2022), and Aronow and Lopatto (2026) study different restrictions. Hammer et al. (1996) supplies only prospective motivation for a complete fixed-horizon binary-endpoint regimen trial; no reanalysis of censored ACTG175 outcomes is claimed.
prose_updates.interpretation: For the planned binary three-regimen contrast \(c^\dagger\), a trialist may use \(q^\dagger\), the total Airy-feedback estimator, and the terminating finite-sample certificate knowing that their second-order value matches the unrestricted optimum even when competing designs may correlate assignments across units. For a bounded endpoint on a fixed real interval \([L,U]\), the observable Bernoulli-polynomial lift gives the same conclusion after multiplying squared risk by \((U-L)^2\). This bounded statement is mathematical rather than an exact-computation claim for arbitrary unrepresented reals.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Unrestricted sharpness is proved at the fixed rational contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), not for every permitted multiarm contrast; accordingly, equality versus strict second-order loss of \(q^\star\) remains open in general. The effective binary certificate uses rational and ordered-algebraic input records, and no representation-independent terminating evaluator is claimed for an arbitrary real contrast, endpoint, or observed value. These are scope limits, not missing steps in the proved \(c^\dagger\) equality or in the exact bounded-risk scaling identity.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The unrestricted sharp theorem and its computable finite-data certificate concern the binary unequal three-arm contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\). The exact endpoint reduction gives a mathematically total bounded-outcome corollary for every fixed real \(L<U\), and the fixed-independent bounded expansion holds for every permitted fixed contrast. The paper does not claim unrestricted sharpness for general \(c\) or a terminating evaluator for an arbitrary real contrast or unrepresented real bounded dataset. At \(c^\dagger\), however, the independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) is proved second-order optimal; the equality-versus-loss question remains open only beyond this established contrast.

statement_notes.justification: The proved dual-score Airy procedure is total on binary labeled data and, together with the unrestricted-estimator Bayes converse for the fixed independent design, yields the exact second-order benchmark for every permitted fixed contrast.
statement_notes.gap: The theorem optimizes estimators under \(q^\star\); it does not by itself settle unrestricted design optimality for a general contrast.
statement_notes.consumer: A trialist can implement the binary benchmark directly and use its separately proved bounded-endpoint lift when the endpoint lies in a fixed interval.

statement_notes.justification: The proved allocation-tube conclusions (A)--(C), exact orbit Bayes lower bound, and matching feasible procedure give the unconditional unrestricted sharp expansion at \(c^\dagger\).
statement_notes.gap: No gap remains at \(c^\dagger\); unrestricted sharpness for general permitted contrasts is outside this theorem.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the binary premise for \(\mathrm{thm:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}bounded\text{-}endpoint\text{-}sharp\text{-}limit\) and the sharp prospective three-regimen benchmark.

statement_notes.justification: The exact-target generalized van Trees ledger proves all local, exterior, and zero-face bounds, while the effective primal construction provides a common computable all-future tail.
statement_notes.gap: No gap remains for the fixed binary contrast \(c^\dagger\); the construction is intentionally binary and contrast-specific.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the proved all-count converse and matching binary procedure used by the sharp-limit and effective-certificate theorems.

statement_notes.justification: The proved allocation tube, exact finite evaluator, and computable primal tail yield terminating binary finite-data brackets converging to the sharp constant.
statement_notes.gap: No proof gap remains for binary \(c^\dagger\); exact effectivity for arbitrary unrepresented real endpoints or observations is outside scope.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the computable binary certificate accompanying the unrestricted sharp expansion.

proofs.proof_tex:
The exact-primitives proposition gives
\(\kappa(c^\dagger)=5/8\) and identifies
\(\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)=\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\) for every labeled schedule in the response-count orbit.  The Airy definition therefore gives
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\in(0,\infty).
\tag{1}
\]
For every sufficiently large \(n\), the root theorem supplies the live positivity certificate
\[
\alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+4\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A})\le\frac12,
\tag{2}
\]
the exact-target all-count bounds, and the effective primal procedure.  The exact-target directional van Trees lemma and the orbit-Bayes lemma therefore apply to the random finite-population target itself.  For an arbitrary outcome-independent design with allocation-count law \(\pi\),
\[
\operatorname{BR}\ge\sum_r\pi(r)\mathcal B(r)
\ge B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}.
\tag{3}
\]
Taking maximum risk and then the minimax infimum proves the middle Bayes inequality in the theorem.

The exact definition gives
\[
n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\}
=\max_rG_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r).
\tag{4}
\]
The local, exterior, and zero-count sets partition \(\mathcal R_{n,3}\); conclusion \({\rm(A)}\) of the root and \((4)\) give the first risk inequality in \((1)\) of the statement.  Conclusion \({\rm(B)}\) gives its last two inequalities because the returned procedure is feasible in the risk game.  Thus
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-.
\tag{5}
\]
Conclusion \({\rm(C)}\) bounds both errors by \(E(N)\) for every \(n\ge N\), proving equation \((2)\) in the statement.  Since \(E(N)\downarrow0\), rearranging \((5)\) and using \((1)\) proves the sharp expansion.  This is the algebraic corollary of the now-proved root conclusions, with no appeal to the legacy scalar prior or to an existential primal remainder.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every integer \(K_0\ge2\), every \(n\ge1\), every pair of fixed real endpoints \(L<U\), every contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^{K_0}\) satisfying \(\sum_{a=1}^{K_0}c_a=0\), and every fixed nonempty class \(\mathfrak D\) of outcome-independent assignment laws, including classes whose laws have arbitrary cross-unit dependence,
\[
 R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,[L,U]}(c)
 =(U-L)^2R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,\{0,1\}}(c).
\tag{3}
\]
For every binary procedure of finite worst-case second moment, the upper-bound map in this equality is a total, nonrandomized estimator given by a finite polynomial in the assignment labels and the observed normalized outcomes.  The equality leaves the design-law class and both estimator infima unchanged.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(s=U-L>0\).  We prove the two inequalities in \((3)\) for the same fixed class \(\mathfrak D\).

For the lower bound, take an arbitrary binary schedule \(x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K_0}\) and form the endpoint schedule \(w=L\mathbf 1+sx\).  The zero-sum condition gives the exact causal-target identity
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a=1}^{K_0}c_aw_{i,a}
 =\frac{L}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a=1}^{K_0}c_a
  +\frac{s}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a=1}^{K_0}c_ax_{i,a}
 =s\tau_c(x).
\tag{4}
\]
Fix \(\mathcal D_n\in\mathfrak D\) and any possibly randomized bounded-outcome estimator \(\delta\).  On binary data define the randomized estimator
\(
\delta_{01}(A,x_A)=s^{-1}\delta(A,L\mathbf1+sx_A)
\).
Equation \((4)\) implies, schedule by schedule,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[
 \{\delta(A,L\mathbf1+sx_A)-s\tau_c(x)\}^2\right]
 =s^2\mathbb E\!\left[
 \{\delta_{01}(A,x_A)-\tau_c(x)\}^2\right].
\]
Endpoint schedules are contained in \([L,U]^{n\times K_0}\).  Taking the binary supremum, then the estimator infimum and the infimum over the unchanged class \(\mathfrak D\), proves
\[
 R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,[L,U]}(c)
 \ge s^2R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,\{0,1\}}(c).
\]

For the reverse inequality, fix \(\mathcal D_n\in\mathfrak D\) and a binary estimator kernel \(K_{01}(du\mid A,\xi_A)\) having finite worst-case second moment.  Let
\[
 m_{01}(A,\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R}u\,
 K_{01}(du\mid A,\xi),
 \qquad \xi\in\{0,1\}^n,
\]
on assignment vectors of positive \(\mathcal D_n\)-probability, and define it arbitrarily on null assignment vectors.  For a bounded schedule \(w\), put \(z_{i,a}=(w_{i,a}-L)/s\in[0,1]\).  Given the realized labels \(A\), independently generate latent variables \(\Xi_{i,a}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(z_{i,a})\), independently also of the estimator seed.  Rao--Blackwellization gives the following explicit observed-data estimator:
\[
 \widehat\tau_{[L,U]}(A,w_A)
 =s\sum_{\xi\in\{0,1\}^n}m_{01}(A,\xi)
   \prod_{i=1}^n
   z_{i,A_i}^{\xi_i}(1-z_{i,A_i})^{1-\xi_i}.
\tag{5}
\]
The right side is a finite polynomial in \(A\) and the observed numbers \(z_{i,A_i}\); hence no unobserved \(w_{i,a}\) is used.  It defines a real number on every observation, after an arbitrary finite definition on assignment-null observations.  Thus it is mathematically total even when the real endpoints or observations have no computability representation.

For each fixed schedule \(w\), outcome independence makes the law of \(A\) independent of the auxiliary array \(\Xi\).  Equation \((4)\), now averaged coordinatewise under \(\Xi\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\Xi}\{\tau_c(\Xi)\}
 =\tau_c(z)=s^{-1}\tau_c(w).
\]
Writing \(\widehat\tau_{01}\) for the action drawn from \(K_{01}\), the definition \((5)\) therefore yields, conditional on \(A\),
\[
 \widehat\tau_{[L,U]}(A,w_A)-\tau_c(w)
 =s\,\mathbb E_{\Xi,K_{01}}\!\left[
 \widehat\tau_{01}(A,\Xi_A)-\tau_c(\Xi)\mid A\right].
\tag{6}
\]
Conditional Jensen's inequality applied to \((6)\), followed by expectation over the possibly dependent assignment vector, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n}
 \{\widehat\tau_{[L,U]}-\tau_c(w)\}^2
 &\le s^2\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,\Xi,K_{01}}
 \{\widehat\tau_{01}(A,\Xi_A)-\tau_c(\Xi)\}^2\\
 &=s^2\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K_0}}
 \Pr_w(\Xi=x)\,
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,K_{01}}
 \{\widehat\tau_{01}(A,x_A)-\tau_c(x)\}^2\\
 &\le s^2\sup_{x\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K_0}}
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,K_{01}}
 \{\widehat\tau_{01}(A,x_A)-\tau_c(x)\}^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
No product or independence condition was imposed on \(\mathcal D_n\); only the auxiliary Bernoulli array is independent.  The zero binary estimator shows that the binary minimax value is finite, so procedures of infinite worst-case second moment may be discarded when taking the infimum.  Taking in \((7)\) the supremum over \(w\), then the infimum over all binary estimator kernels and over the same \(\mathcal D_n\in\mathfrak D\), proves
\[
 R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,[L,U]}(c)
 \le s^2R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,\{0,1\}}(c).
\]
Together with the endpoint lower bound, this proves \((3)\) and every asserted quantifier-preservation and observability clause.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the two-treatment finite-population experiment with fixed binary potential outcomes, squared-error loss for the average treatment effect, and optimization over every assignment mechanism and measurable estimator, the unrestricted minimax risk equals \(\rho_n^\star\).  For fixed real \(L<U\), the corresponding unrestricted game with potential outcomes in \([L,U]\) has minimax risk \((U-L)^2\rho_n^\star\).  Moreover,
\[
 \rho_n^\star=\frac1n-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),
\]
where \(C_A=-4^{1/3}a_1'>0\) and \(a_1'\) is the largest negative zero of the derivative of the Airy function.

source.locator: Theorems 2.2, 2.3, and 3.1 (unrestricted binary equality, exact bounded scaling, and Airy expansion) of arXiv v1

attestation.note: Checked directly against arXiv:2608.13822v1. Theorem 2.2 identifies the unrestricted binary procedure game, Theorem 2.3 gives exact bounded-endpoint scaling, and Theorem 3.1 gives the Airy expansion.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the binary three-arm game at \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), restriction of nature to schedules satisfying \(Y_i(2)=Y_i(3)\) for every \(i\) gives exactly the published unrestricted two-treatment game:
\[
 \inf_{\mathcal D_n,\widehat\tau}
 \max_{\substack{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times3}:\\Y_i(2)=Y_i(3)\ \text{for every }i}}
 \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n}\!\left[
 \{\widehat\tau-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\right]
 =\rho_n^\star.
\tag{8}
\]
Both the assignment law and the estimator, including randomized estimators, are unrestricted in \((8)\).  Consequently,
\[
 R_n(c^\dagger)\ge\rho_n^\star
 =\frac1n-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\tag{9}
\]
Because
\(C_A>C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), the imported bound \((9)\) is asymptotically strictly weaker than the sharp three-arm lower bound and cannot supply its second-order coefficient.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write a schedule in the restricted class as
\(
Y_i(1)=Y_i^{(1)}
\) and
\(
Y_i(2)=Y_i(3)=Y_i^{(0)}
\).  The coefficient identity \(-1/4-3/4=-1\) gives
\[
 \tau_{c^\dagger}(y)
 =\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{Y_i^{(1)}-Y_i^{(0)}\},
\tag{10}
\]
which is the two-treatment finite-population average treatment effect.

First take any two-treatment procedure.  Embed it in the three-arm experiment by assigning arm \(1\) whenever the two-treatment label is one and arm \(2\) whenever that label is zero, never assigning arm \(3\), and applying the same estimator.  Equation \((10)\) shows equality of risk on every restricted schedule.  Taking infima proves that the left side of \((8)\) is at most \(\rho_n^\star\).

Conversely, fix an arbitrary outcome-independent three-arm assignment law and an arbitrary randomized labeled-data estimator.  Put
\[
 B_i=\mathbf1\{A_i=1\}.
\]
The induced joint law of \(B=(B_1,\ldots,B_n)\) is an admissible outcome-independent two-treatment design and may have arbitrary cross-unit dependence.  Because the state spaces are finite, for every \(b\) of positive induced probability there is a conditional law
\(
Q(a\mid b)=\Pr(A=a\mid B=b)
\)
supported on labels satisfying
\(
\mathbf1\{a_i=1\}=b_i
\).  Given two-treatment labeled data, a randomized two-treatment estimator can draw \(A'\sim Q(\cdot\mid B)\) and then apply the original three-arm estimator to \(A'\) and the same observed outcomes.  On the restricted schedules, the observed outcome is \(Y_i^{(1)}\) when \(B_i=1\) and \(Y_i^{(0)}\) when \(B_i=0\), regardless of whether \(A_i'=2\) or \(3\).  Hence the simulated two-treatment data and action have exactly the same joint law as the original three-arm data and action, schedule by schedule.  If the cited two-treatment game is written with nonrandomized estimators, replacing this simulated action by its conditional mean can only decrease squared-error risk by conditional Jensen.  Thus \(\rho_n^\star\) is no larger than the risk of the arbitrary three-arm procedure.  Taking its worst case and then its infimum proves the reverse inequality in \((8)\).

The full nature class contains the restricted one, so \((8)\) and the published two-treatment Airy expansion give \((9)\).  The established sharp-limit theorem gives the three-arm coefficient \(C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\).  Since \(C_A>0\) and \(0<5/8<1\),
\[
 C_A-C_A(5/8)^{2/3}
 =C_A\{1-(5/8)^{2/3}\}>0.
\]
Thus the lower-risk benchmark on the right of \((9)\) subtracts a strictly larger second-order constant and is strictly weaker for all sufficiently large \(n\), proving the final claim.

added_lemmas.statement:
For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\) and every pair of fixed real endpoints \(L<U\), the unrestricted design-estimator minimax risk for schedules in \([L,U]^{n\times3}\) obeys the exact finite-sample reduction
\[
 R_{n,[L,U]}(c^\dagger)
 =(U-L)^2R_{n,\{0,1\}}(c^\dagger)
 =(U-L)^2R_n(c^\dagger),
\tag{11}
\]
and hence the sharp expansion
\[
 R_{n,[L,U]}(c^\dagger)
 =(U-L)^2\left\{
 \frac1n-C_A(5/8)^{2/3}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})
 \right\}.
\tag{12}
\]
The polynomial lift in \(\mathrm{lem:multiarm\text{-}bounded\text{-}endpoint\text{-}reduction}\) turns every total binary finite-data procedure into a mathematically total procedure on the bounded real observation space.  No exact Turing-computability claim is made for unrepresented real endpoints or observations.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Apply \(\mathrm{lem:multiarm\text{-}bounded\text{-}endpoint\text{-}reduction}\) with \(K_0=3\), \(c=c^\dagger\), and \(\mathfrak D\) equal to the class of all outcome-independent assignment laws on \(\{1,2,3\}^n\).  Its exact equality and \(\mathrm{def:bounded\text{-}risk\text{-}game}\) give \((11)\), preserving arbitrary assignment dependence and all randomized-estimator quantifiers.

The established binary theorem \(\mathrm{thm:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}sharp\text{-}limit}\) gives
\[
 R_n(c^\dagger)
 =\frac1n-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),
 \qquad
 \Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}.
\]
Multiplication by the fixed positive constant \((U-L)^2\) preserves the \(o(n^{-4/3})\) remainder, proving \((12)\).  The totality and non-effectivity clauses follow directly from the finite polynomial formula \((5)\) in the reduction lemma.

proposed.construction:
For an integer \(K_0\ge2\), write \(\mathcal A_{K_0}=\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\).  Fix \(n\ge1\), real numbers \(L<U\), a contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^{K_0}\), and a nonempty class \(\mathfrak D\) of assignment laws on \(\mathcal A_{K_0}^n\), every member of which is selected independently of the potential-outcome schedule.  For \(\mathcal I=[L,U]\) or \(\mathcal I=\{0,1\}\), define
\[
 R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,\mathcal I}(c)
 =\inf_{\mathcal D_n\in\mathfrak D}\ \inf_{\delta}
   \sup_{w\in\mathcal I^{n\times K_0}}
   \mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,\delta}\!\left[
   \left\{\delta\bigl((A_i,w_{i,A_i})_{i=1}^n\bigr)
   -\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a=1}^{K_0}c_aw_{i,a}
   \right\}^2\right],
\]
where the second infimum is over all possibly randomized Markov kernels from the labeled observed data to \(\mathbb R\), and the expectation includes both assignment and estimator randomization.  Write these two risks as \(R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,[L,U]}(c)\) and \(R^{\mathfrak D}_{n,\{0,1\}}(c)\).  When the first infimum ranges over all outcome-independent assignment laws, abbreviate them by \(R_{n,[L,U]}(c)\) and \(R_{n,\{0,1\}}(c)\), respectively.  For every permitted contrast satisfying \(\sum_ac_a=0\) and \(\sum_a|c_a|=2\), projection to \([-1,1]\) cannot increase squared loss, so \(R_{n,\{0,1\}}(c)=R_n(c)\) in the binary game of \(\mathrm{def:risk\text{-}game}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Defines the fixed-class bounded and binary games needed for the exact endpoint reduction without changing the binary kernel.
